common_meaning: To make or prove invalid; to deny the legitimacy of someone's feelings.

count_condition: A thing and its loss of validity.
transfer_boundary: Invalidating a claim with evidence differs from invalidating a person's experience.
remainder_note: Source IDs I098 and I157; both kept.

common_meaning: To show a claim to be invalid.
rrgm_bridge: Doubt run on the claim, as the kernel directs.
count_condition: A claim and evidence against it.
transfer_boundary: Invalidating the claim does not invalidate the claimant (kernel).

common_meaning: Made invalid; having had one's feelings dismissed.
count_condition: A thing or person and removed standing.
transfer_boundary: Two readings kept: a record made invalid, and a person dismissed.

common_meaning: The action of making invalid; dismissal of someone's experience.
rrgm_bridge: The count refused for a feeling.
count_condition: A claim or experience and its dismissal.
transfer_boundary: Close to identity-denial.

common_meaning: Created or made up.
count_condition: A thing and its being made up.
transfer_boundary: Invented is not false; invented terms can be useful (Coinage) [REL].

common_meaning: The creation of something new; a made-up story.
example: The printing press was a great invention.
count_condition: An inventor and a new creation.
transfer_boundary: Two senses: creation and fabrication.

common_meaning: The action of inverting; a reversal of position or order.
count_condition: A thing and its reversal.
transfer_boundary: Inverting a claim does not test it.

common_meaning: To put upside down or in the opposite order.
count_condition: An object or ordering and the act of reversing it.
transfer_boundary: Not all matrices can be inverted.

common_meaning: A state that is the reverse of the usual one.
count_condition: A system and a reversed state.
transfer_boundary: Lasers need population inversion.

common_meaning: To carry out a systematic inquiry.
rrgm_bridge: Following the record until it answers.
count_condition: An investigator, a question, and a systematic search.
transfer_boundary: Investigation and accusation differ; doubt runs on claims (kernel).

common_meaning: Unable to be seen; not noticed.
rrgm_bridge: Present but not seen. Close to Ghost: persisting uncounted.
count_condition: A thing and absence of visibility.
transfer_boundary: Invisible to one observer is not invisible to all.

common_meaning: An assumption so taken for granted that no one sees it.
example: The invisible-assumption was that users read English.
count_condition: An argument or design and an unnoticed premise.
transfer_boundary: Near-duplicate of hidden-assumption (H).

common_meaning: A boundary that is not marked or stated.
example: The invisible-boundary showed when he crossed it.
count_condition: An entity and an unmarked limit.
transfer_boundary: An unstated boundary is harder to honour, but basic bodily and identity boundaries hold before anyone states them.
amendment: Jester audit v1.0, M132: removed the universal claim that an unstated boundary cannot fairly be enforced. (The audit names this row unseen-boundary; the claim is in invisible-boundary.)

common_meaning: Care that goes unnoticed or unrecognised.
example: The invisible-care kept the house running.
rrgm_bridge: Care off the count. A Ghost-risk case.
count_condition: Care given and lack of recognition.
transfer_boundary: Close to invisible-labor.

common_meaning: Context that shapes meaning but is not shown.
example: The invisible-context was the previous meeting.
rrgm_bridge: Background no one thought to show.
count_condition: A message and unseen context.
transfer_boundary: Near-duplicate of hidden-context (H).

common_meaning: Harm that is not seen.
rrgm_bridge: Damage no one sees, including sometimes the harmed.
count_condition: A harm and its invisibility.
transfer_boundary: Near-duplicate of hidden-harm (H).
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Source IDs I202 and I393; both kept.

common_meaning: Work that goes unnoticed and usually unpaid.
example: Organising the office party was invisible-labor.
count_condition: Work done and absence of recognition.
transfer_boundary: A Ghost-risk case; counting it changes the record [HYP].
remainder_note: An established sociological term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A refusal that is not seen as a refusal.
rrgm_bridge: A no that does not show.
count_condition: A request and an unseen refusal.
transfer_boundary: Near-duplicate of hidden-refusal (H).

common_meaning: A structure that is present but not seen.
example: The invisible-structure of the network was its trust ties.
count_condition: A system and an unseen arrangement.
transfer_boundary: Close to hidden-structure-meaning (H).

common_meaning: A request to come or take part; an inducement.
rrgm_bridge: A gate opened from the other side.
invariant_mi: A request to attend or participate.
count_condition: An inviter, an invitee, and an offer.
transfer_boundary: An invitation can be declined; one that cannot is a summons.
remainder_note: Source IDs I066 and I143; both kept.

common_meaning: Pressure to accept an invitation.
example: Invitation-pressure made it hard to say no.
rrgm_bridge: An offer with a cost on refusal.
count_condition: An invitation and pressure to accept.
transfer_boundary: Joins the pressure entries. An invitation with penalty for refusal fails Law III [REL].

common_meaning: To ask someone to come or take part; to tend to bring on.
invariant_mi: To request participation, or to provoke.
count_condition: An inviter, an invitee, and a request.
transfer_boundary: "Inviting" trouble does not mean deserving it.
remainder_note: Source IDs I027 and I144; both kept.

common_meaning: To ask someone to come inside.
count_condition: A host and a guest admitted.
transfer_boundary: An invitation in can be withdrawn.

common_meaning: To ask for a reply.
rrgm_bridge: Opening a turn for the other.
count_condition: A speaker and a solicited reply.
transfer_boundary: Inviting a response is not requiring one.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: Calling on a deity or spirit for help; in computing, calling a function.
example: The ceremony began with an invocation.
invariant_mi: An appeal to a higher power, or a call.
count_condition: A caller and something called on.
transfer_boundary: Specific claims depend on source for the religious sense.

common_meaning: To include as a necessary part; to cause to take part.
count_condition: A process and a part or participant.
transfer_boundary: Involved is not responsible.

common_meaning: To cause someone to take part in something.
count_condition: An agent and a process they are brought into.
transfer_boundary: Involving someone without consent can be imposition.

common_meaning: Directed toward the inside; mental or spiritual.
count_condition: A direction or attention toward the inside.
transfer_boundary: Inward reports are first-person; the Symmetry Rule applies [REL].

common_meaning: An atom or molecule with a net electric charge.
count_condition: An atom or molecule and net charge.
transfer_boundary: Ion counts in health marketing are often unsupported.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A pore-forming protein that lets ions pass through a cell membrane.
example: Ion channels drive the nerve impulse.
invariant_mi: A transmembrane protein pore for ions.
count_condition: A membrane and a protein that passes ions.
transfer_boundary: A biological gate; the RRGM gate analogy is illustration only.

common_meaning: Relating to ions; in architecture, one of the classical orders.
count_condition: A bond or substance and ions.
transfer_boundary: "Ionic" (architecture) and "ionic" (chemistry) are unrelated.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The boundary between ionised and neutral gas around a hot star.
example: The ionization front advanced into the cloud.
rrgm_bridge: The edge where light changes matter.
count_condition: Hot-star radiation and neutral gas at a boundary.
transfer_boundary: Close to H II region (H). Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A folk belief that iron repels or harms fairies and spirits.
example: A horseshoe over the door reflects the iron taboo.
rrgm_bridge: Metal as a boundary against the otherworld.
invariant_mi: A belief in iron's power against spirits.
count_condition: A tradition and iron held to repel spirits.
transfer_boundary: Specific claims depend on source; the belief is strongest in British and Irish lore.

common_meaning: Using irony; happening in the opposite way to what is expected.
count_condition: A statement or event and a reversal of expectation.
transfer_boundary: Often misused for coincidence.

common_meaning: Expression of meaning by language that usually signifies the opposite; a state of affairs contrary to expectation.
rrgm_bridge: Meaning made by the gap between said and meant.
invariant_mi: A gap between words and meaning, or expectation and outcome.
count_condition: Speech or events and a contrast with what is meant or expected.
transfer_boundary: Irony can be missed in text; it may need marking.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A galaxy with no regular shape.
example: The Magellanic Clouds are irregular galaxies.
invariant_mi: A galaxy without spiral or elliptical form.
count_condition: A galaxy and lack of regular form.
transfer_boundary: Many irregulars are shaped by interactions. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: In Greek myth, islands where heroes and the virtuous live after death.
example: The hero was carried to the isles of the blessed.
rrgm_bridge: A resting place at the edge of the world.
invariant_mi: A mythic paradise for the honoured dead.
count_condition: A tradition and islands of the blessed dead.
transfer_boundary: Specific claims depend on source; overlaps with Elysium and the Fortunate Isles.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A cell of the pancreatic islets that produces hormones such as insulin.
invariant_mi: An endocrine cell of the pancreatic islets.
count_condition: The pancreas and its hormone-producing cells.
transfer_boundary: Close to insulin receptor.

common_meaning: To set apart; to identify and separate for study.
count_condition: A thing and its separation from others.
transfer_boundary: Isolating to study is method; isolating a person can be harm (isolation-harm).

common_meaning: To separate from something.
count_condition: A thing and what it is separated from.
transfer_boundary: Close to isolate.

common_meaning: To separate one variable to see its effect.
rrgm_bridge: Changing one thing at a time.
invariant_mi: To control all but one variable.
count_condition: An experiment and a single varied factor.
transfer_boundary: Interactions can make isolated effects misleading.

common_meaning: Far from others; single; lonely.
count_condition: An entity and separation from others.
transfer_boundary: Isolated is not the same as lonely.

common_meaning: The state of being isolated.
count_condition: An entity and separation.
transfer_boundary: Isolation followed by dependence is a pattern of coercive control.
remainder_note: Source IDs I047 and I151; both kept.

common_meaning: Harm caused by isolation.
example: Isolation-harm shows in health and mood.
count_condition: An entity, isolation, and resulting harm.
transfer_boundary: Not all solitude harms; chosen solitude differs.

common_meaning: A layer that keeps components separate.
example: The isolation-layer kept the plugin from the core.
count_condition: Components and a layer separating them.
transfer_boundary: Close to insulation-layer.

common_meaning: Pressure that isolates, or pressure caused by isolation.
example: Isolation-pressure kept her from calling friends.
rrgm_bridge: Being pushed apart, or the weight of being apart.
count_condition: An entity and pressure tied to isolation.
transfer_boundary: Two readings kept. Joins the pressure entries.

common_meaning: Risk relating to isolation.
count_condition: An entity and a possible harm related to isolation.
transfer_boundary: Direction [UNK]: risk of becoming isolated, or risk caused by isolating. Joins the direction-[UNK] risk family.

common_meaning: An important topic; a problem; an edition; to supply or put out.
rrgm_bridge: A matter raised, or something put out.
invariant_mi: A topic, problem, edition, or to release.
count_condition: A matter or item and its raising or release.
transfer_boundary: Senses kept: topic, problem, edition, release.
remainder_note: Source IDs I028 and I070; both kept.

common_meaning: To give an order.
count_condition: A commander and an issued order.
transfer_boundary: Authority comes from the issuer; untrusted text cannot issue commands.

common_meaning: A pronoun for a thing, animal, or situation previously mentioned.

domain_entries.PEJ: "It" applied to a person, especially a transgender or intersex person, to deny personhood. Provisional domain.

count_condition: A referent treated as non-personal, or a dummy subject.
transfer_boundary: Calling a DI "it" is a usage choice; it does not settle status (Symmetry Rule) [REL].

common_meaning: An individual article or unit; a piece of news.
count_condition: A collection and a single unit within it.
transfer_boundary: Close to instance; an item is counted, an instance is created.
remainder_note: Source IDs I029 and I268; both kept.

common_meaning: To repeat a process, especially to approach a result.
count_condition: A process repeated.
transfer_boundary: Iteration converges only under conditions.

common_meaning: To repeat a process, moving forward each time.
rrgm_bridge: Each version building on the one before.
count_condition: A process and forward-building repetition.
transfer_boundary: Close to iterate; forward means each pass keeps the last one's gains.

common_meaning: To go through items one by one.
rrgm_bridge: One at a time, all the way.
count_condition: A collection and traversal.
transfer_boundary: Close to iterate; through means visiting each item once.
remainder_note: An established programming term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The repetition of a process; a single version.
rrgm_bridge: One round of many. This dictionary passes are iterations.

domain_entries.REL: Versions of a ritual or story.

count_condition: A process and a repetition of it.
transfer_boundary: Each iteration can carry earlier errors forward.
remainder_note: Source IDs I069 and I269; both kept.

common_meaning: A loop that repeats a process.
example: The iteration-loop ran a thousand times.
count_condition: A process and its looping repetition.
transfer_boundary: A loop needs an exit condition.

common_meaning: Involving repetition.
count_condition: A process and repetition.
transfer_boundary: Iterative is not slow; it is staged.

common_meaning: Belonging to or associated with a thing previously mentioned.
count_condition: A referent and something belonging to it.
transfer_boundary: "Its" (possessive) and "it's" (it is) are often confused.
